title: Bookkeeper Administrator
description:
Part-Time Bookkeeper / Administrator

Location: Maidstone, Kent
Hours: 20 hours per week (flexible working pattern available)
Salary: £30,000 - £35,000 pro rata (dependent on experience)
Contract: 12-month fixed-term contract with the possibility of extension

Overview

A well-established Maidstone-based accountancy practice is seeking a reliable and detail-oriented Bookkeeper / Administrator to join their team on a part-time basis. This is a 12-month fixed-term contract, with the potential to be extended, and would suit an experienced bookkeeping professional looking for flexibility while playing a key role in supporting a varied client portfolio.

Key Responsibilities
- Maintain accurate financial records for a portfolio of clients
- Process day-to-day bookkeeping including:
- Sales and purchase ledger
- Bank reconciliations
- Petty cash reconciliation
- Prepare and submit VAT returns
- Assist with the preparation of management accounts
- Liaise with clients to resolve queries and collect financial information
- Process payroll (if experience held - desirable but not essential)
- Maintain and update accounting systems (e.g. Xero, QuickBooks, Sage)
- Assist senior accountants with year-end accounts preparation
- Ensure compliance with relevant financial regulations and deadlines
- Support general administrative duties within the practice

Person Specification

Essential:
- Previous experience in a bookkeeping or accounts assistant role (ideally within a practice environment)
- Strong knowledge of bookkeeping principles
- Experience with accounting software such as Xero, Sage or QuickBooks
- High level of accuracy and attention to detail
- Ability to manage workload and meet deadlines
- Good communication skills and client-facing experience

Desirable:
- AAT qualified or part-qualified (or equivalent)
- Experience working within an accountancy practice
- Payroll experience

Key Skills & Attributes
- Organised and methodical approach
- Proactive and able to work independently
- Strong IT skills, including Excel
- Professional and personable manner
- Flexible and adaptable

title: Credit Controller
description:
German Speaking Commercial Collector
- Location: Maidstone
- Salary: £28,000 basic £45,000 OTE
- Hours: 9am-5pm (with discretionary flexibility)
- Job Type: Full-time, Office Based

Join a dynamic team as a German Speaking Commercial Collector. This role is crucial for maximising cash collections through both inbound and proactive outbound calls. Fluency in GERMAN is essential to effectively manage international and domestic debts.

Day-to-day of the role:
- Negotiate early repayment of international and domestic debts.
- Update debtor management systems accurately.
- Recommend next steps to clients after failed collection attempts.
- Escalate disputes to Client Services swiftly.
- Maintain accurate records and workflows.

Required Skills & Qualifications:
- Proven background in commercial credit control or B2 B collections, or sales/customer service experience with a desire to move into collections.
- Confidence on the phone and working towards financial targets.
- Fluency in German - essential for the role.
- Effective communication skills.
- Strong influencing and negotiating skills.
- Ability to build rapport and focus on customer needs.
- Team player who is articulate, literate, numerate, and possesses excellent keyboard skills.

Benefits:
- Competitive salary with generous monthly bonus potential - up to £1,400/month.
- 20 days holiday + bank holidays, rising to 25 days.
- Pension scheme: 3% employer contribution, 5% employee contribution.
- 2 canteens with free hot drinks and water.
- Weekly treats including snacks and protein bars.
- Breakout area with pool table, table tennis, and darts.
- Beautiful office location near Maidstone town centre.

Interested?

Apply now and join a supportive, high-performing team!

title: Purchase Ledger Clerk (Temporary)
company: Pearson Whiffin Recruitment Ltd - Agency - Permanent
description:
We are currently recruiting on behalf of a well-established client based in Maidstone who is looking for an experienced Purchase Ledger Clerk to join their busy finance team on an ongoing temporary basis.

Due to an increase in workload, they are looking for someone who can hit the ground running and provide support across the Purchase Ledger function.

Key responsibilities will include:
- Matching, batching and coding a high volume of supplier invoices
- Matching invoices against purchase orders and delivery notes
- Carrying out payment reconciliations
- Investigating and resolving invoice and payment queries
- Ensuring invoices are processed and paid within agreed payment terms
- Maintaining accurate Purchase Ledger records
- Liaising with suppliers and internal departments where required
- Supporting the wider finance team with ad-hoc duties as required

About you:

The successful candidate will have previous experience working within a Purchase Ledger / Accounts Payable role and be confident working in a fast-paced, high-volume environment.

You will have good attention to detail, strong organisational skills and be comfortable dealing with invoice and supplier queries.

This is an ongoing temporary position with no confirmed end date, working full-time Monday to Friday. Our client is looking for someone to start as soon as possible, so candidates who are immediately available or available at short notice would be particularly suited to the role.

If you have the Purchase Ledger experience we're looking for and are available to start at short notice, apply today!

title: Administrative Assistant
company: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
advertiser_name: Kent and Medway Mental Health NHS Trust
description: Are you a dedicated, compassionate Admin Assistant? Do you want the chance to help shape a new and genuinely innovative service for care in Kent and Medway? You will be providing direct admin support to members of the clinical team and to the new Centralised Health Based Place of Safety. We are an adaptive, cross-functional service. Whilst being assigned to directly support a department, you will be providing support (as a team) throughout the Directorate. Teamwork is an essential part of this role, good time-keeping and the ability to keep to deadlines and adapt your way of working are vital. As a support service, we adapt to the needs of the service; we are regularly reviewing ways of working and optimising our internal processes. We need someone who can think on their feet and adapt to day-to-day circumstances as they arise. If this sounds like the opportunity you have been waiting for, come and join our diverse and compassionate team committed to delivering excellent care and support for service users and their loved ones. ** Please note, Visa sponsorship is not available for this role.** This role provides direct administrative support to our in-patient care, Management, Consultant Psychiatrist, Lead clinicians and the wider team. The successful candidate will work closely with the teams: Providing up-to-date information to the teams and producing simple report Maintaining patient records Creation and maintenance of spreadsheets and internal forms within designated timescales Maintaining and updating displays Scheduling clinical meetings Diary and meeting management Generic team mailbox monitoring and maintenance and any other administrative duties requested Please see the attached job description for full details of the main duties and responsibilities of the role.
